description.content: OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint and flow-engine callback.

Initiates an OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization flow. On success, redirects the user-agent
to the login page. On error, redirects to the client's registered redirect_uri or the
server error page. When `request_uri` is provided (PAR), the stored parameters are used
instead of the inline query parameters.

query.description: (Required) Must be `code` for the authorization code flow.
OAuth 2.0 response mode. When omitted, query mode is used by default. Only query mode is supported. Requests with unsupported values such as fragment or form_post are rejected with invalid_request.
The URI to redirect to after authorization.
Opaque value to maintain state between the request and callback.
String value used to associate a client session with an ID token.
Reference URI to a pushed authorization request (RFC 9126).

Resource indicator per RFC 8707 (absolute URI, no fragment). Only one value is supported; requests with multiple resource values are rejected with invalid_target. When omitted from a permission-bearing request, the configured defaultResourceServer is used. OIDC-only and scopeless requests use the client_id audience.
Requested Authentication Context Class Reference values.

Space-separated list of prompts (OIDC Core §3.1.2.1). Supported values: `login` forces re-authentication; `consent` forces re-consent for all required attributes regardless of existing consent records.

response.name: Redirect to the login page or the client redirect_uri on error.
Bad Request — malformed or duplicate query parameters.

description.content:
Internal endpoint invoked by the flow engine after a successful authentication ceremony.
The flow engine submits a signed assertion JWT; this endpoint validates it, issues an
authorization code, and returns the redirect URI for the client.

response.name: Authorization code issued. The redirect_uri includes the code and state.
Bad Request — missing or invalid authId / assertion.

description.content: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint for issuing access tokens, refresh tokens, and ID tokens.

Issues access tokens, refresh tokens, and ID tokens. Supports the following grant types:
`authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, `refresh_token`, `password`,
`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693), and
`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` (draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant).
Requires client authentication via HTTP Basic auth or `client_id`/`client_secret` form parameters.

Token exchange additionally supports requesting an Identity Assertion Authorization Grant
(ID-JAG) by setting `requested_token_type` to
`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag`, with `subject_token_type` set to
`urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token` and a single required `audience` value matching
one of the client's configured `allowedAudiences`. The `resource` parameter is optional and,
when present, is embedded in the issued ID-JAG for the resource authorization server to
process. Requires the client to be confidential and to have ID-JAG issuance enabled
(`token.idJag.enabled`) on its application configuration. The response has
`issued_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag` and `token_type=N_A`, since the
issued value is a JWT authorization grant rather than an access token.

The `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` grant presents an ID-JAG assertion (obtained
from a trusted external IdP) via the required `assertion` parameter, and exchanges it for a
ThunderID access token. Optional `scope` and `resource` parameters further narrow the granted
scopes and audience; `resource` must be a subset of the assertion's own `resource` claim when
the assertion carries one. No refresh token is issued for this grant.

Returns metadata about a token. If the token is invalid, expired, or revoked, the
response will contain `"active": false` with no other fields. Implements RFC 7662.
Requires client authentication.

Token revocation per RFC 7009.

Revokes a previously issued access or refresh token. On success the server responds with
HTTP 200 and an empty body. A token that cannot be validated — bad signature, malformed, or
unknown — is treated as a successful no-op per RFC 7009. Expired tokens with a valid
signature remain revocable. Requires client authentication; a client may only revoke tokens
issued to it. Implements RFC 7009.

urlencoded.description: (Required) The access or refresh token to revoke.
Hint about the type of the submitted token (`access_token` or `refresh_token`). Accepted per RFC 7009 §2.1 but optional; ThunderID tokens are self-describing, so the hint does not affect processing.

response.name: Token revoked, or a no-op success for a token that cannot be validated. Empty body.

description.content: (Required) The access or refresh token to revoke.

response.name: Bad Request — the token parameter is missing (`invalid_request`), or the token was issued to a different client (`invalid_grant`).

JSON Web Key Set endpoint for token verification.
Returns the server's public keys in JWKS format for verifying signed tokens.

description.content: OIDC UserInfo endpoint for retrieving claims about the authenticated user.

Returns claims about the authenticated end-user. The access token must be sent in the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The response is a JSON object or a signed/encrypted
JWT depending on the client's registration settings. Implements OIDC Core §5.3.

response.name: Unauthorized — missing or invalid Bearer token.

description.content:
Identical to the GET variant but accepts the access token via HTTP POST body or
`Authorization` header per OIDC Core §5.3.2.

response.name: Unauthorized — missing or invalid Bearer token.

description.content: Dynamic Client Registration per RFC 7591.

Registers a new OAuth 2.0 / OIDC client. When DCR is not configured as insecure, a
valid access token with system-level permissions is required. Implements RFC 7591.

response.name: Unauthorized — missing or insufficient access token (when DCR is not insecure).

description.content: OpenID Connect Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) endpoint.

Initiates an OpenID Connect Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) request in
poll mode. The client identifies the user with exactly one of `login_hint` or `id_token_hint`
(`login_hint_token` is defined by the specification but not supported and is rejected with
`invalid_request`), and the server begins an out-of-band authentication ceremony. The returned
`auth_req_id` is polled at the token endpoint using the `urn:openid:params:grant-type:ciba`
grant. Requires client authentication.

RFC 8707 resource indicators bind the request to a single resource server before user
authorization. A valid `resource` binds the request to that resource server; when omitted from
a permission-bearing request the configured `defaultResourceServer` is used, and a
permission-bearing request with no resource and no default is rejected with `invalid_target`.
OIDC-only requests without a resource remain valid and keep the `client_id` audience. Multiple
`resource` values, including duplicates, are rejected with `invalid_target`. The resulting
access token has the bound resource server identifier as its sole `aud`, and its permissions
are limited to those defined by that resource server. A `resource` optionally supplied when
polling the token endpoint must exactly match the bound resource server.

OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect protocol endpoints. Covers authorization, token issuance, token introspection, pushed authorization requests, dynamic client registration, JWKS, and the OIDC UserInfo endpoint.
